S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within five business days. They must notify the affected unit’s customer within 48 hours, or sooner when needed to reduce an immediate safety risk, and provide known hazards, safe-use or isolation instructions, and available corrective actions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before initial market placement and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A failure rate above 5% requires a documented corrective-action plan submitted to regulators within 60 days and retesting within six months; it does not by itself prohibit continued sale while the plan is being implemented.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all new units placed on the market beginning 24 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit pathway for installed units and complete retrofits within six years of the effective date, where technically feasible.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required on all new units placed on the market beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers must document compliance using a regulator-approved method and provide compliance information to regulators and customers.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must notify regulators, submit supporting data and a corrective-action plan within 30 days, and contact affected customers without undue delay with appropriate safety guidance. Exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory regulatory review and corrective action; it does not by itself require a recall.

document.section_notes: S1 is strict: all incidents reported within 24 hours and customers notified within 48 hours. S2 keeps a 55 °C test and 5% threshold but allows continued sales with corrective action, provides results to customers but not the public. S3 requires new-unit shut-off after 24 months and retrofit within 6 years where feasible; S4 requires built-in suppression after 36 months; S5 makes 8/100k a review/corrective-action trigger, not an automatic recall, with prompt notices and regulator discretion.
